key_insight: For semilinear parabolic PDEs, neural approximation costs separate into governing-law complexity and data encoding, helping explain why modest networks can approximate infinite-dimensional solution operators.
engineering_relevance: Structure-aware architectures can keep parameter costs independent of grid resolution and time step, with only logarithmic nonlinear-block cost for two-dimensional Navier–Stokes.
method: Represent the constitutive law with a neural block whose complexity depends on its computation graph.
Encode data using a bounded number of learned weights per mode.
Derive trajectory-level approximation bounds and near-matching lower bounds for viscous Hamilton–Jacobi equations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical approximation guarantees, including roughly η^(-1/s) parameter scaling for C^s Hamiltonians and a matching lower bound up to logarithms, rather than empirical benchmark results.
watch_item: Resolution-independent parameter bounds do not imply resolution-independent runtime or guaranteed success when training these architectures.
paper_title: Neural Network Approximation and Structural Complexity of Semilinear PDEs with Lower Bounds
